analysis.investment_thesis: Affle has built an impressive mobile advertising platform serving emerging markets with a performance-based CPCU model, compounding revenue and profits at 45% CAGR over 7 years while remaining nearly debt-free with growing free cash flow. The business has attractive unit economics, but at 47x trailing P/E and 40x EV/EBITDA, I am paying a premium for a moat in ad-tech — a sector where Google and Meta hold structural dominance and where today's platform advantage can evaporate quickly.
key_strengths: Exceptional financial compounding: 45% revenue CAGR and 45% net profit CAGR over 7 years with OCF positive all 5 of the last 5 years and FCF growing to 266 Cr in FY25
Near debt-free (D/E 0.01) with 1,047 Cr cash on balance sheet — the company is self-funding its growth without diluting shareholders, which I deeply respect
CPCU (cost per converted user) performance model creates advertiser alignment and differentiation from impression-based ad networks, with scale advantages in emerging market data
key_risks: Ad-tech is a structurally competitive industry dominated by Google and Meta; Affle's moat — while real today — is less durable than brand moats or switching-cost moats in industrial businesses
ROE of 14% falls below my 15% threshold despite 45% growth, suggesting the serial acquisitions (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) are diluting capital returns even as they add revenue
At 47x P/E, any slowdown in the 40%+ growth trajectory — due to macro, competition, or platform algorithm changes — will result in severe multiple compression
red_flags: ROE of 14% below my 15% floor despite exceptional revenue growth — the acquisition-heavy growth strategy is consuming equity without commensurate return improvement
Operating margin of 18.1% is modest for a technology platform; gross margin of 29% is low, suggesting meaningful traffic acquisition costs that constrain profitability expansion
Goodwill and intangibles from multiple acquisitions are likely a large component of the 3,914 Cr asset base — a 1,047 Cr cash pile against 3,256 Cr equity implies significant intangible assets
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Affle is one of the more interesting technology businesses I have reviewed from India. The CPCU model — charging only for converted users — is a sensible performance contract that aligns incentives and creates a measurable value proposition. The consistent 45% revenue and profit growth while remaining debt-free is genuinely admirable execution by management. The 266 Cr FCF in FY25, up from near-zero a few years ago, shows the business is maturing and beginning to generate real owner earnings.

However, I am cautious about paying 47x earnings for an ad-tech business, no matter how well-run. The advertising industry is ultimately subject to the gravitational pull of the largest platforms, and Affle's 18% operating margin leaves less room for error than I prefer. The company has made five significant acquisitions — Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi — and while these appear well-integrated, each acquisition resets the clock on organic moat building. I would find this business significantly more attractive at 25–30x earnings, where I would be getting the growth at a price that offers some margin of safety.
